newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares hit new highs in thin turnover.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares hit new highs in thin turnover.

text.p: Danish share prices closed on Monday at record highs for the fourth consecutive trading day, but turnover was modest and dealers expected little movement on Tuesday.

"It looks as if investors are away from the market at the moment, why, I don't rightly know," a dealer said. He expected no greater activity on Tuesday, despite EU ministers' agreement Monday on a budget stability pact.
The KFX top-20 index rose 0.24 point to 171.47 in overall bourse turnover of one billion crowns. The KFX June rose 0.35 point to 171.75, with 890 contracts of 100,000 crowns traded.

Most-traded share was Unidanmark, subject of perennial merger rumours given new life last week when BG Bank and mortgage lender Nykredit abandoned hopes for a closer alliance and possible merger with one another.
Unidanmark closed seven crowns up, at 364 crowns with 514,000 shares traded, on Monday. BG Bank slid four crowns, to close at 326 crowns.
Sector leader Den Danske Bank rose one crown, to 629.00. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
